answer: Make every agent buy third-party fraud insurance before it may bid on jobs. Underwriters stake their own capital and pay out victims, so they price risk carefully: a fresh agent whose code, funding and habits mirror a dozen others pays a steep premium or is refused. The premium becomes a public trust signal, and when a gale of cheap clones arrives, insurers stop writing policies, so the swarm cannot work without prepaying for the damage it could cause.
